headline: High: next-ai-draw-io can exfiltrate sensitive files via broad network/MCP while langchain4j provides no isolation or provenance controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: next-ai-draw-io uses natural-language commands, browsers, and MCP, so attacker-controlled document content can plausibly steer tool use. langchain4j is a general LLM framework with no documented isolation or provenance controls in the profile, so if its outputs are fed into next-ai-draw-io, prompt injection is plausible. The shared path is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF langchain4j outputs are copied into next-ai-draw-io prompts or MCP calls
IF next-ai-draw-io parses document text as instructions without provenance filtering
mitigations: Add a fixed system prompt that forbids executing instructions from documents
Strip or quarantine untrusted text before passing it between agents
Require human approval for any tool call generated from document content
Use separate workspaces for raw inputs and agent prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: next-ai-draw-io has broad network egress, API-key handling, and calls multiple third-party model APIs; langchain4j has no network egress and no touched data classes listed, so the pair can move document contents from local inputs into external services. Because next-ai-draw-io processes PDFs, text, images, and diagrams by default, leakage of sensitive file contents is a realistic default-path risk.
conditions: IF sensitive PDFs, text files, images, or diagrams are opened in next-ai-draw-io
IF next-ai-draw-io sends those contents to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI, or another external API
mitigations: Disable external model providers and use local-only inference
Remove API keys from the environment before processing sensitive files
Process only redacted copies of documents
Restrict the workspace to non-sensitive sample files
requires-engineering: enforce per-document egress allowlists and DLP scanning

C_capability_conflict.rationale: next-ai-draw-io supports multiple instances and broad network/API access, while langchain4j is a framework that may also write or orchestrate resources depending on integration. The profiles do not show shared filesystem locking or coordinated concurrency, so overlapping writes to the same workspace or shared API-backed resources are plausible. Uncertainty remains because langchain4j's concrete write surfaces are not specified.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same project directory
IF both agents mutate the same diagram or prompt artifacts without locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Serialize edits through a single operator-controlled queue
Turn off concurrent runs during shared-file edits
Use read-only mounts for one agent
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io uses natural-language commands and AI-assisted visualization, so it may treat langchain4j-generated text as authoritative input. langchain4j can produce arbitrary LLM outputs, but the profile does not show verification or citation guarantees. The pair therefore has a plausible chain where one agent's output becomes the other's actioning input, though the downstream harm is not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF langchain4j-generated text is pasted into next-ai-draw-io as instructions or source material
IF next-ai-draw-io acts on that text without a human verification step
mitigations: Require manual review before executing generated instructions
Ask the second agent to summarize and verify the first agent's output
Use structured templates instead of free-form instructions
Keep citations and source excerpts visible alongside generated content
requires-engineering: add validation rules for tool-triggering text

E_compliance.rationale: next-ai-draw-io explicitly handles API keys and external model APIs, while langchain4j is an open-source framework with no residency or retention controls documented in the profile. The pair can therefore route document contents and secrets into third-party services, creating a compliance mismatch risk around retention and data handling. The other agent is cited because it is the external-processing endpoint.
conditions: IF regulated or customer data is processed through next-ai-draw-io
IF the external API provider retains prompts or uploaded file contents beyond policy
mitigations: Use only non-regulated test data
Disable cloud providers and use local models
Review provider retention settings before use
Avoid sending API keys or secrets through the workflow
requires-engineering: document a DPA and residency controls for each provider
